plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: DE and TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative: Six aldosterone-treated vs six vehicle-control human kidney samples, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired. The question asks which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response. The plan follows the grounded bulk RNA-seq procedure end to end in Python: (1) sample-structure QC on a variance-stabilized matrix to confirm the samples separate by condition and to catch outliers before any test; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter followed by pydeseq2's built-in median-of-ratios normalization and a Wald test of treated vs control, with an explicit reference level (control) so a positive log2FC means higher in treated; (3) apeglm-style shrinkage of the fold change and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 to call DE genes; (4) TF activity inference with decoupleR's univariate linear model (ulm) run on the DESeq2 Wald statistic of every tested gene against the CollecTRI human regulon staged in the reference store — this is the central deliverable, since a prior-knowledge regulon on 6-vs-6 counts is the only sound TF-activity method at this sample size (an ARACNe/VIPER-style network needs far more replicates); (5) a Hallmark GSEA pass on the same ranked statistic for pathway-level context around the TF findings; (6) a consolidated report with QC/fit diagnostics, the DE table (raw and shrunken LFC), the ranked TF activity table (top TFs by |ulm score| with FDR), enrichment results, and full reproducibility metadata (package versions, regulon version, seed).

condition ~ 1 + condition, reference level = vehicle/control, contrast condition treated vs control

decoupler ulm on Wald stat with CollecTRI human regulon
gseapy prerank GSEA on Wald stat with MSigDB Hallmark human
summary report with QC, DE, TF activity, enrichment results, session info
apeglm log fold change shrinkage (via pydeseq2 DeseqStats.lfc_shrink)
